name: Pinnote – Website Feedback
author: Pinnote

sections.description:
Pinnote is website feedback for freelancers, agencies and product teams. Your clients click the thing they want changed, or drag over an area, and type a note. It arrives in your Pinnote inbox with a screenshot of exactly what they saw, with the spot marked, plus the page address, the element, and their browser and screen size. Nobody has to ask “which page, which button?” again.

This plugin adds Pinnote to your WordPress site. Paste your site key and you’re done: no code, no theme edits.

For your clients

  • No account, no password and no browser extension. They open the link you send and comment.
  • Pin a note to any element, drag to mark an area, or leave a general comment about the page.
  • Your replies show up next to their note, on the page.
  • Visitors see nothing. Only people you invite, people with your share link, or everyone on pages you open to reviewers get the Feedback button.

For you and your team

  • One inbox for every note, with priority, labels, assignment and team-only notes.
  • A reviewer can confirm a fix looks right, or reopen it.
  • Screenshots never show what people typed in forms. Emails, phone numbers and card numbers are hidden too.
  • Export to CSV or a printable report.
  • On Pro: Slack, signed webhooks, and GitHub issues (closing the issue resolves the note).
  • Connect Claude Code, Codex or Cursor through Pinnote’s MCP server, and your coding agent can read each note with its screenshot, fix it, reply and resolve it.

Works with any theme and page builder, including Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder and the block editor, and on staging sites.

Pricing

Pinnote is free for one site, with unlimited reviewers and 50 open notes. Pro is $9 a month or $90 a year for unlimited sites, notes and history, for your whole team. See pricing.

External services

This plugin connects your site to Pinnote, a hosted feedback service, which is needed for it to work. It loads the Pinnote widget from https://pinnote.app/widget.js on your site’s public pages, and the widget talks to pinnote.app to show and save feedback. Nothing is loaded or sent until you save a site key.

For visitors who aren’t reviewers, the widget only checks whether they should see the Feedback button. When a reviewer leaves feedback, Pinnote receives what they write, a screenshot of the page as they saw it (with typed text hidden), the page address, the element they pointed at, their screen size and browser, and the name (and optional email) they give.

  • Service: Pinnote
  • Terms of Service
  • Privacy Policy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Sign up at pinnote.app, add your site, and copy its site key. It starts with pk_.
  3. In WordPress, go to Settings › Pinnote, paste the key and save.
  4. In Pinnote, invite your client by email or copy your share link, and send it to them.

The full guide: Install Pinnote on WordPress.
sections.faq:
Will my visitors see a feedback button?

No. Only people you invite, people with your share link, or everyone on pages you’ve opened to reviewers in Pinnote.

Do my clients need a WordPress or Pinnote account?

No. They open the link you send them and comment. They don’t need to log in to WordPress either.

Does it slow my site down?

The widget loads after the page, asynchronously, and does nothing for visitors who aren’t reviewers.

Can I use it on a staging site?

Yes. Add the staging address to your site in Pinnote, or add it as its own site, and install the plugin there.

Is it free?

Pinnote is free for one site with unlimited reviewers. Pro is $9 a month for unlimited sites.

How do I turn it off?

Clear the site key in Settings › Pinnote, or deactivate the plugin. Deleting the plugin removes its setting.
